problem_units.macro_problem_name: Domain Adaptation and Generalization and Action-Sensitive Visual and Motion Representation
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can image-pretrained VLMs distinguish action-sensitive objects from static background objects?
problem_units.failure_mode: The image encoder attends to static object semantics and overlooks objects involved in motion or action.
problem_units.root_cause: Image-text pretraining lacks temporal action cues and creates a domain gap with video grounding.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: Late fusion adds motion after image encoding and cannot deeply adapt the image encoder to action-sensitive regions.
problem_units.affected_scenario: A lady is drinking coffee; the image encoder should attend to the mug and the hand holding it.

evidence.quote: However, being pre-trained on massive image-text data, VLM tend to focus on the semantics of static objects.

problem_units.macro_problem_name: Sparse Evidence Discovery in Long Videos and Compositional and Explicit Temporal Reasoning
problem_units.micro_problem_name: End-to-end VLM adaptation on long raw videos is computationally impractical
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can a VLM image encoder be adapted in-domain before downstream grounding without end-to-end long-video training?
problem_units.failure_mode: Jointly training the feature encoder and downstream model on long raw videos incurs prohibitive cost.
problem_units.root_cause: The adaptation target is a large pretrained image encoder while the downstream input is long video.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: Ordinary end-to-end fine-tuning couples feature adaptation with expensive downstream temporal training.

evidence.quote: Firstly, trivial end-to-end fine-tuning is impractical because it requires training the feature encoder and the downstream model concurrently on long raw videos, resulting in extremely high computational overhead.

method_units.macro_method_name: Structured and Agentic Reasoning Mechanisms and Domain Adaptation Mechanisms
method_units.micro_method_name: Preliminary in-domain VLM feature adaptation with pairwise ranking and contrastive pretext tasks
method_units.method_core_mechanism: Fine-tune only a small part of the VLM image encoder on downstream-domain clips before standard grounding.

evidence.quote: Consequently, we introduce an efficient in-domain feature adaptation strategy.

method_units.macro_method_name: Reconstruction-Discrepancy Mechanisms and Representation Learning Mechanisms
method_units.micro_method_name: Action-Cue-Injected prompt learning with video-guided and verb-guided prompts
method_units.method_core_mechanism: Produce action cues from video and text encoders and inject them as prompt embeddings into the VLM image encoder.

evidence.quote: First, Action Cue Injection module (ACI) facilitates VLM to capture action-sensitive patterns from images under the guidance of action cues from other modalities.

method_units.macro_method_name: Multi-Scale Context Modeling and Data Augmentation and Context Diversification
method_units.micro_method_name: Context-aware Temporal Prompt Learning over selected action-sensitive regions
method_units.method_core_mechanism: Select action-sensitive regions from consecutive frames, extract motion features, and turn them into temporal prompts.
method_units.what_is_transferred_or_injected_or_align: motion information from consecutive action-sensitive regions

evidence.quote: After identifying action-sensitive visual regions via attention scores in individual images, we introduce Context-aware Temporal Prompt Learning (CTPL), which extracts motion features from a temporal sequence of selected visual regions in consecutive frames, considering the temporal context.
